# Reviewing models with no lifestyle-sustaining match · 0.38.0

All 28 public cases that lacked a lifestyle-covering option in release 0.37.0 were reviewed individually. The six owner-only cases already had a covering option; their replay remains outside public source. The review compares current interests, recent histories, field preferences, follow-up answers and every one of the 117 catalog careers against the unchanged first-paid-stage budget.

## Result

Five models regain related exploration options. Twenty-one retain a starting-pay shortfall within the currently evidenced catalog, and two have open, undifferentiated interests. Current public no-coverage count: 23, down from 28. With the six private cases included, 131 of 154 models have an exploration option covering the selected budget. This is a software-scenario count, not measured recommendation accuracy.

- Aisha Ellery: data science and statistics. Eight analysis-task choices were blocked by incomplete confirmation of a broad technology field partly described in software/device terms. The restored options have about $956 and $135 monthly room respectively under the saved budget.
- Linh Cabrera: animation. Seven relevant visual-storytelling choices were blocked by incomplete broad creative-field confirmation. The restored option has about $169 monthly room and remains a related idea requiring a project/portfolio trial.
- Gabriel Soto-Ruiz: school psychology and occupational therapy. The related search omitted the teaching careers actually displayed after a tie in the original engine. Restoring those seeds recovers related options, with clinical/assessment training and role differences explicit.
- Imani Westbrook: website/interface and product design. Film editing was displayed but omitted as a related-search seed. Content/usability is a reasonable trial; physical product design has little direct task evidence and must remain explicitly unconfirmed.
- Audrey Whitfield: project coordination, human resources and logistics. The displayed administrative-assistant option was omitted as a search seed. Coordination/office preferences justify exploration, while weak settled academic preferences and the differences in business duties call for new work samples. HR only narrowly covers the budget.

## Narrow repairs

The original engine's answers, six RIASEC scores and profession rankings remain unchanged. Wages, training costs, budget assumptions and the displayed Top matches remain unchanged. Only the supplemental related-option paths change:

1. Related search uses the same supported Top matches selected by the student presentation, including ties resolved for display. Shared selection is factored into match-selection.js; the original engine list remains available for audit.
2. A role can remain a related task option when broad-field confirmation is incomplete if its field follow-ups are complete and it has at least six selected question groups, three refinement groups, four focused answers, two evidence domains, some positive destination-field evidence and interest-profile correlation at least 0.20. Existing field, clinical-role, training-route and flat-profile exclusions remain. The label stays Related match; it does not become a direct or automatic choice.

No case IDs or biographies occur in eligibility logic. Income cannot create task evidence. The rule also retains lower-paying relevant choices for Cora, Miles, Nadia, Zara and Rafael without changing their no-coverage result. Recovered options are not guaranteed employment, salaries or validated fits.

## Remaining outcomes

The individual web review records the evidence, examined careers, pay/budget results, judgment and next useful check for every original case. Examples of legitimate gaps include Mateo's repair interests versus a $75K goal, Marisol's product-design pay versus $70K, writing/media budgets above entry references, and River's $120K home-ownership-plus-saving scenario. River's “modest home” narrative is not translated into a cheap budget: the saved scenario includes a $300,000 home, a financed used car and $1,500 monthly saving. Lee's $320K target is not supported by any catalog first-paid-stage scenario and also retains a responsibility/training-route conflict.

Remy's equal moderate totals and no task choices, and Charlie's equal high totals plus broad enthusiasm, do not establish differentiated career preferences. Their lower budgets are not the reason for empty results. Supportive work introductions are the appropriate next step.

## Catalog follow-ups and external evidence

Technical writing, purchasing/buying and training/development warrant their own catalog coverage and focused task questions. Accurate explanation, product/stock comparison and teaching interests provide reasons to investigate; they are not proof of a new affordable match. Dedicated Austin entry wages, prerequisites and experience requirements have not been verified for these additions, so no national median is substituted and none is counted as recovered coverage.

- Data science duties and study: https://www.bls.gov/ooh/math/data-scientists.htm
- Animation duties and storyboards: https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/27-1014.00
- Technical writing: https://www.bls.gov/ooh/media-and-communication/technical-writers.htm
- Purchasing/buying: https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/purchasing-managers-buyers-and-purchasing-agents.htm
- Training/development: https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/training-and-development-specialists.htm

Reproduce the public snapshot with build-model-match-chart.mjs, then build-no-match-review.mjs. Case judgments are in research/no-match-review-038/case-notes.json; generated budgets and outcomes are in validation/no-match-review-038.json. These are interpretive case reviews of fictional profiles, not a real-student calibration study.

The reviewed cases include both development and previously held-out cases. Because this repair was informed by them, they now establish regression behavior for this revised layer, not independent holdout performance. Fresh untouched profiles are required for the next matching-quality evaluation.

The full 3,276 model/career screening comparisons are retained in validation/no-match-catalog-scan-038.json. Reproduce them with node scripts/review-no-match-catalog.mjs; positive budget room is separated from interest evidence and prerequisite experience.

Verification: the full 521-test suite passed before the final completion guard, and all 24 focused tests passed afterward, including a new pre-review Top-list comparison (522 distinct passing tests). All 148 displayed Top lists match the saved 0.37.0 baseline. The six owner-only cases still have coverage. The public-output scan found none of 79 private biography fragments.

Browser checks confirm review filtering, desktop and 390px phone layout, and Aisha’s recovered data-science/statistics options in the actual isolated student view.
